name: Mailchimp Multi-Step Form
description: This template makes it easy to grow your email and newsletter subscriber list within no time.

14.label: This form template uses the Mailchimp addon
14.description: With the Mailchimp addon, you can connect WPForms to your Mailchimp account to automatically add subscribers to your mailing lists when they fill out your form. Before you publish this form, go to the Marketing tab to the left and: [] Install and activate the Mailchimp addon. [] Connect your Mailchimp account to WPForms using your Mailchimp API key. [] Choose your Mailchimp account, audience, and the action you wish to perform. [] Map your form's fields to your Mailchimp account. If you're new to this addon, see our Mailchimp addon documentation for full details. For more help, contact our support team.
14.expanded-description:
In addition to adding new subscribers to your lists, the Mailchimp addon enables your users to unsubscribe or delete their information from your account, providing a seamless, user-friendly experience.
You can also segment your subscribers by adding users to different lists in your Mailchimp account. You'll be able to add Mailchimp tags and notes to your subscribers as well, providing helpful data about your users right in your email marketing account.
Last but not least, if you have custom fields set up in Mailchimp for unique subscriber information, you can map them to fields in your form to automatically collect that data.

12.label: Lead Forms Enabled
12.description: Your form has been converted to a lead form. Learn how to format it for maximum impact.
12.expanded-description: If you scroll down and look at your form, you'll notice that page breaks have been inserted after each field. Lead forms typically have 1–3 fields per page, so this will help you get your new lead form up and running quickly. Follow the tips below to optimize your lead form. These are completely optional, but will yield the best results! [] Create big, bold headings. Instead of using standard field labels, try using page titles. Click on a Page Break to add a page title. Be sure to hide each field's label in its field options as well. [] Consolidate pages, if necessary. Each field is now on its own page, but you may want to group similar fields on the same page. Drag and drop fields to reorganize them, then delete any Page Breaks you no longer need. [] Use icon choices for radio buttons. Upgrade your standard Multiple Choice field radio buttons to fancy icon choices that look great and convert. [] Use placeholders instead of sublabels. Some fields (Name, Address, etc.) have sublabels. Trying using placeholder text instead. For more lead forms tips and best practices, check out our Complete Guide to Lead Forms.
